clue.text: Stand about next to a member in staging area

parts.note: a stand or support is a base
C is short for circa, Latin for about
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A support placed beside a politician somewhere theatrical, as if setting up a stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staging area' and 'Stand' both pull towards the theatre; here the staging area is where climbers gather before an ascent.
explanation.definitionFit: Mountaineers use the lowest camp as the place where expeditions assemble and stock up before pushing on.

clue.text: One short, beneath stream, makes gesture

definitions.note: a phrase meaning the verb, in the same third-person form as the clue reads it

indicators.note: in a down entry the shortened word is placed below the stream

parts.note: a beck is a stream in northern England

indicators.note: short means the word for one loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as the word one

explanation.surface: A golfer one shot short, below a stream, waves.
explanation.walkthrough: BECK is a northern English word for a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: To signal someone to come closer with a wave of the hand is to make a gesture.

clue.text: Son also wearing tartan trousers in university town

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

indicators.note: the tartan trousers are worn around the word for also, enclosing it

parts.note: trews are close-fitting tartan trousers, traditional Scottish dress
and means also

explanation.surface: A son also dressed in tartan trousers in a Scottish university town.
explanation.walkthrough: TREWS are Scottish tartan trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fife town holds Scotland's oldest university, founded in 1413, and is also the home of golf.

clue.text: In consideration, R&A constructed protective barrier

indicators.note: constructed means the letters are assembled into something new

parts.note: taken as written
the R&A, Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews, gives the letters R and A

explanation.surface: After deliberation, the R&A, golf's governing body, built a protective barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: The R&A governs golf outside the USA and Mexico and runs the Open.
explanation.definitionFit: A French term for a guarded line set up to stop a disease spreading, or a buffer zone in politics.

clue.text: Position for cricketer round Irish golf club

indicators.note: the fielding position goes round the letters for Irish, enclosing them

parts.note: mid-on is a cricket fielding position on the leg side near the bowler

explanation.surface: A fielder's spot near an Irish golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: MID-ON is a cricket fielding position, straight-ish on the batter's leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: A club in the middle of a golfer's set, used for medium-distance shots, is a type of golf club.

clue.text: Complaint from a scholar crossing street close to Medinah

indicators.note: the scholar's letters straddle the street and the letter after it, so they sit on either side

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, here of Medinah

explanation.surface: An academic walks across a road near Medinah, the US golf course, and catches something.
explanation.walkthrough: Medinah is a golf course near Chicago that has hosted major championships.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint is a medical word for an illness, and this breathing disorder is one example.

clue.text: Sees tall verbose foreign golfer

indicators.note: foreign means alien or strange, so these letters are made unfamiliar by rearrangement

explanation.surface: A tall, wordy golfer from abroad sees things.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spaniard won five majors, including three Opens, and is among the greatest golfers of all time.

clue.text: Robust and tough — McIlroy, ultimately

parts.note: hard means tough

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of McIlroy

explanation.surface: Rory McIlroy, the Northern Irish golfer, ultimately proves robust and tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturdy plants or people that survive harsh conditions are robust, a close synonym.

clue.text: An Open champion, with individual lacking power

parts.note: and means with, in addition to

indicators.note: lacking means the individual is without the letter for power

parts.note: a person is an individual
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: An Open winner, playing with someone short of power.
explanation.walkthrough: Jamie Anderson, a Scot, won the Open three years running, 1877 to 1879.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamie, the nineteenth-century Scottish golfer, took the Open Championship three times in a row.

clue.text: Birdies from balls going further than intended?

definitions.meaning: birdies are little birds, things that fly
in golf, a shot that flies too far, often from the rough, earns this name

explanation.surface: Golf scores one under par come from shots that overshoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Birdies' looks like golf scores; it is birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds are creatures that fly; golfers give the same name to balls that fly beyond their target.

clue.text: Burn restricts one in lead

indicators.note: the scorching word holds the numeral within its bounds, confining it

parts.note: to char is to burn or scorch
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A burn, a Scottish stream, hems in a golfer who is leading the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burn' reads as a Scottish stream, a hazard on links courses; here it is the verb to scorch.
explanation.definitionFit: To preside over a meeting or committee is to lead it, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Distributed as it happens — take in action

indicators.note: the broadcasting word and the letter for take are put inside the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an action
a live broadcast is shown as it happens
R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on old prescriptions

explanation.surface: Something handed out in real time, with a demand to grab a share of the action.
explanation.walkthrough: R for 'take' comes from the Latin 'recipe' heading a doctor's prescription.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that have been distributed have been handed over or brought to people, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Former road leading to this at 2, the "home of golf"

parts.note: old means former, as in an old flame
a course is a route or way taken, like a road

explanation.surface: An old road leads to the famous links at St Andrews, the home of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 refers to the answer at 2-down, ST ANDREWS, the Scottish town whose oldest links are called the home of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: The oldest links at St Andrews, in Fife, are widely celebrated as the birthplace of the game.

clue.text: Charles, say — Bob's initial start in Open ends in bogey, birdie, par

indicators.note: an initial is the opening letter of a name, here of Bob
the start of a word is its first letter, here of Open
the ends of the three golf scores are their final letters

explanation.surface: Bob Charles, the 1963 Open champion, starts his Open with bogey, birdie, par.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Charles' the golfer Bob Charles; as a definition it is the actor Charles Boyer.
explanation.definitionFit: The French film actor Charles Boyer is an example of someone with this surname.

clue.text: Admiral Byron, for example

definitions.meaning: Horatio, victor at Trafalgar, the best-known British admiral
Byron of that surname was a great American golfer of the 1930s and 40s

explanation.surface: A naval officer named after the poet Lord Byron.
explanation.walkthrough: Byron suggests the poet, but in this golfing puzzle it is the American golfer Byron Nelson.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are a surname: the famous admiral killed at Trafalgar and the golfer Byron, winner of eleven straight events.

clue.text: Real upset on Troon's last in very good battle

indicators.note: the shuffled letters and the extra one go inside the word for very good

parts.note: so can mean very, and an old crossword sense of so is very good

indicators.note: upset means the letters of Real are knocked into a new order
the last of a word is its final letter, here of Troon

explanation.surface: Real Madrid upset on Troon's final hole, where the Open was played, in a very good fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Troon is a Scottish links course that hosted the Open in 2016.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian port gives its name to the 1943 Allied landings and fighting there in the Second World War.

clue.text: Rest hint about heading for Augusta

indicators.note: the hint goes about the letter, surrounding it

parts.note: a reminder is a hint or prompt

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, here of Augusta

explanation.surface: A golfer takes a break before heading for Augusta, home of the Masters.
explanation.walkthrough: Augusta National in Georgia hosts the Masters.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left over once part is taken is the rest, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Part of golf club: small society inside for dance

indicators.note: the two abbreviations sit inside the pair of words for and dance

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a hop is an informal dance
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A small society meets inside part of the golf club for a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The shop run by the resident professional, selling equipment, is a fixture of a golf clubhouse.

clue.text: Takes umbrage at fees across south-east

indicators.note: the payments stretch across the compass letters, enclosing them

parts.note: rents are fees paid for the use of property
SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed by charges applied across south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: To be aggrieved by something is to take umbrage at it, so the phrases are synonyms.

clue.text: Draw off Hoylake's first so pin seen differently

indicators.note: seen differently means these letters are viewed in another arrangement
the first of a word is its opening letter, here of Hoylake

explanation.surface: At Hoylake, the Royal Liverpool links, a hole's pin position looks different.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoylake is the home of Royal Liverpool Golf Club, an Open venue.
explanation.definitionFit: To drain liquid away through a tube is to draw it off, a close synonym.

clue.text: Louise's partner extremely tough male put out

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outer letters, here of tough
put out means the letters of male are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A tough man is upset by Louise's partner.
explanation.definitionFit: In the 1991 film, Louise's companion on the road trip is this character, played by Geena Davis.

clue.text: Girl in group, upset smothering her approach at first

indicators.note: smothering means covering on both sides, so the turned word encloses her
in a down entry upset means turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a set is a group
taken as written

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of approach

explanation.surface: A girl in a group is upset and smothers her approach shot at first.
explanation.definitionFit: A common girl's name, as with Mother Teresa or the politician May, so a girl.

clue.text: Small rocky island in part of Munster, below course's fifth

indicators.note: in a down entry the county comes below the letter
the fifth letter of course

parts.note: Kerry is a county in Munster, Ireland's south-western province

explanation.surface: A small island lies off part of Munster, below the fifth hole of a golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: KERRY is a county in the Irish province of Munster.

clue.text: Quiet, with a newspaper, in part of golf club

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
FT, the Financial Times, this crossword's own newspaper

explanation.surface: A quiet word, read in a newspaper, inside part of the golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golf club' suggests a clubhouse; it is the club swung, whose long handle is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The long handle of a golf club, joining grip to head, is a structural part of it.

clue.text: Complete round on Oakmont, finally making cut

parts.note: all means complete or whole
O is round in shape

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of Oakmont

explanation.surface: A golfer completes a round at Oakmont, the Pennsylvania course, and makes the cut at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making cut' reads as golf's halfway cut; 'cut' here means to share out.

clue.text: Played with others at Scottish town where 8 once won the Open

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for played in sports league tables
the rest means the others

clue.text: A German playing through gap gets an ace

ein is German for a
on means playing, as an actor is on stage

clue.text: Golf trophy donor's proviso, reportedly

explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Ryder, an English seed merchant, donated the cup contested between Europe and the USA.

clue.text: Pressure to speak in golf club

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
to utter is to speak

clue.text: Faded second of drives, next to spectator

parts.note: passé means faded or past its prime

indicators.note: the second of a word is its second letter, here of drives

parts.note: by means beside or next to

explanation.surface: A golfer's faded drive lands next to someone watching.
